newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's says electronic system test goes well.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's says electronic system test goes well.

text.p: Lloyd's of London said it conducted a successful stress test of an electronic system aimed at speeding up the completion of business done in the insurance market.
"It was a resounding success. Underwriters said they found it very easy to use, very quick and very responsive," Lloyd's spokesman, Oliver Steele, told Reuters on Tuesday.
Electronic Placing System Support (EPS-S) allows underwriters and brokers to record policy details electronically, thus reducing repetitive typing as well as the volume of paper in the market.
During the test, which ran for 15 minutes this morning, the equivalent of 698 insurance business transaction were completed by 153 underwriters on 131 Lloyd's insurance syndicates.
Ninety percent of underwriters were able to access the system within five seconds, Steele said.
The test was carried out at the request of Lloyd's underwriters, who have found earlier versions of EPS slow and difficult to use.
EPS was first introduced in the early 1990s, but usage has fallen well short of expectations, with only around one percent of business being put through it.
The latest version, EPS-S, has been developed in conjunction with market practitioners and retains the so-called paper slip as the base of contract.
Steele said it was hoped that today's test will lead to much greater confidence in EPS-S and therefore a sharp increase in its usage in the September and October insurance renewals season.
Lloyd's will contribute 8,000 stg to charity following the stress test, Steele said.
